description: Build Yalla, a production-grade Go CLI for Dokploy that is first-class for AI agents, covers every Dokploy OpenAPI operation, ships as native cross-platform binaries, and has a strong verification loop.
productPrinciples: AI-agent-first behavior is a product requirement, not a mode added later.
Every Dokploy OpenAPI operation must be reachable through a deterministic CLI interface.
Human-friendly curated commands may exist, but raw API coverage must always remain complete.
JSON output, error codes, exit codes, and schemas are public compatibility contracts.
Normal users and agents must not need Go installed because releases ship native binaries.
No MVP shortcuts. Every story must include meaningful verification.

diagrams.productFlow:
flowchart TD
  A["Dokploy OpenAPI"] --> B["Yalla operation registry"]
  B --> C["Go HTTP client"]
  B --> D["Cobra command tree"]
  D --> E["Curated commands"]
  D --> F["Raw API call commands"]
  E --> G["Human output"]
  F --> H["Agent JSON output"]
  H --> I["Stable schemas and exit codes"]
diagrams.verificationFlow:
flowchart TD
  A["Implement story"] --> B["Format"]
  B --> C["Static checks"]
  C --> D["Unit tests"]
  D --> E["Command tests"]
  E --> F["Golden JSON tests"]
  F --> G["Contract tests"]
  G --> H["Race/security checks"]
  H --> I["Release dry run"]

technologyStack.config: Small internal config layer, optionally backed by koanf if complexity justifies it
technologyStack.http: net/http with typed client wrappers, explicit timeouts, context cancellation, and redaction

agentContract.stdoutRule: Data only. Never progress or diagnostics.
agentContract.stderrRule: Logs, prompts, warnings, progress, and errors only.
compatibilityRules: Adding optional JSON fields is a minor version change.
Removing or renaming JSON fields is a major version change.
Changing exit-code meanings is a major version change.
Changing command or flag meanings is a major version change.

requiredAssertions: manifest operation count matches OpenAPI operation count
every OpenAPI operation has at least raw API coverage

apiOperationStoryAcceptanceCriteriaTempl: Registry entry exists for the operation.
Raw API command executes the operation by operationId.
Schema command returns machine-readable input/output schema.
JSON success and error envelopes follow the Yalla agent contract.
Command tests assert stdout/stderr separation and exit codes.
Contract tests use httptest fixtures and do not require a live Dokploy server.

userStories.title: Bootstrap the Yalla Go module and Cobra root command
userStories.description: Create the production Go project skeleton for the yalla binary with Cobra as the command framework and a testable root command.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a Go module for Yalla with cmd/yalla/main.go as the binary entrypoint.
Use github.com/spf13/cobra as the command framework and keep command construction injectable for tests.
Root command exposes --json, --no-input, --config, --base-url, --token, --verbose, and --version where appropriate.
Data is written to stdout and logs, prompts, warnings, and errors are written to stderr.
Root command has unit tests using in-memory stdout and stderr buffers.
go test ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt, goimports, and go mod tidy pass.
userStories.notes: Start here. This story creates the skeleton every API story depends on.

userStories.title: Implement agent-first output, error, and exit-code contracts
userStories.description: Build the shared output and error packages that make the CLI safe for AI agents and scripts.
acceptanceCriteria: Create internal/output for JSON envelopes, table output, and raw output helpers.
Create internal/errors with stable error codes, user messages, hints, and exit-code mapping.
All --json success responses use schema_version yalla.output.v1.
All --json errors use schema_version yalla.error.v1 and include code, message, and optional hint.
Secrets are redacted in human and JSON output.
Tests prove stdout contains only data and stderr contains errors/progress only.
userStories.notes: This is the most important agent-first contract.

userStories.title: Implement configuration and authentication layers
userStories.description: Load deterministic configuration and credentials for Dokploy API access.
acceptanceCriteria: Config precedence is CLI flags > environment variables > config file > defaults.
Support YALLA_BASE_URL, YALLA_TOKEN, YALLA_CONFIG, YALLA_OUTPUT, and YALLA_NO_INPUT.
Add yalla config get --json and yalla config set commands.
Add yalla auth status --json and a non-leaky token validation path.
Do not print tokens or credentials in logs, errors, or tests.
Config tests cover precedence, missing auth, invalid base URL, and --no-input behavior.
userStories.notes: Do not spread config reads through command code. Load once and pass typed config down.

userStories.title: Implement OpenAPI operation registry and schema extraction
userStories.description: Convert Dokploy OpenAPI metadata into a stable runtime registry used by raw API calls, schemas, manifests, docs, and tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Registry includes all 450 operations from /Users/juribadev/projects/poc/dokploy/openapi.json.
Every registry entry includes operationId, method, path, tag, request schema reference, parameters, response codes, and auth requirement.
Schema commands can emit input schema and output schema for each operation as JSON.
Manifest output lists every operation and can be consumed by an AI agent.
Tests fail if operation count or operation IDs drift from openapi.json without updating the registry.
userStories.notes: OpenAPI sha256: 09999cf46fa7504ca2bc7539d8b1e6817da3d612964a5f83fe404dd32c56c7c7

userStories.title: Implement the raw API executor for full Dokploy coverage
userStories.description: Expose every OpenAPI operation through a deterministic raw API command so no API feature is missing.
acceptanceCriteria: Add yalla api operations --json.
Add yalla api call <operationId> --input request.json --json.
Support path, query, and body inputs without interactive prompts when --no-input is set.
Support --dry-run to print the resolved request without sending it.
Handle HTTP status mapping into stable Yalla error codes.
Tests cover a successful call, a validation failure, a 401 error, a 500 error, and a network timeout.
userStories.notes: This is the universal safety net for all Dokploy APIs.

userStories.title: Implement Dokploy HTTP client with auth, timeouts, and typed responses
userStories.description: Build the shared API client used by raw and curated commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Use net/http with explicit timeout and context cancellation support.
Attach auth token consistently without leaking it in logs.
Parse JSON success and error responses into typed structures.
Preserve response metadata useful to agents, including request id or trace headers when available.
Retries are bounded and only used for safe idempotent operations.
httptest.Server tests cover auth header, request body, response parsing, timeout, cancellation, and redaction.
userStories.notes: Keep HTTP behavior testable without a live Dokploy server.

userStories.title: Implement manifest, schema, and command documentation commands
userStories.description: Expose machine-readable command metadata so AI agents can discover and verify capabilities before acting.
acceptanceCriteria: Add yalla manifest --json with command tree, flags, schemas, exit codes, and operation coverage.
Add yalla schema list --json and yalla schema get <operationId> --json.
Add markdown docs generation for human documentation.
Add shell completion generation for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell.
Tests verify manifest JSON is stable and contains every API operation.
userStories.notes: AI agents should be able to inspect capabilities without scraping help text.

userStories.title: Implement the CLI verification harness
userStories.description: Create the reusable test harness and golden testing approach required by every command story.
acceptanceCriteria: Create test helpers for executing Cobra commands with in-memory stdin, stdout, and stderr.
Add helpers for asserting JSON validity, schema_version, stdout/stderr separation, and exit codes.
Add golden file workflow for stable JSON and selected human output.
Add httptest fixtures for Dokploy API contract tests.
Document how Ralph should run focused and full verification loops.
userStories.notes: Do this before adding many operation stories so later work stays consistent.

userStories.title: Implement release, packaging, and cross-platform distribution
userStories.description: Set up the production release pipeline for native Go binaries and package-manager channels.
acceptanceCriteria: Add GoReleaser config for macOS, Linux, and Windows binaries.
Publish GitHub Release artifacts with checksums.
Prepare Homebrew tap formula generation.
Prepare Scoop and WinGet metadata generation.
Prepare npm/npx wrapper packages that execute the native Go binary while preserving args, stdout, stderr, and exit code.
goreleaser check and goreleaser release --snapshot --clean pass locally or in CI.
userStories.notes: Normal users and agents must not need Go installed.

userStories.title: Implement channel-aware upgrade commands
userStories.description: Support safe update checking and upgrades without breaking package-manager ownership.
acceptanceCriteria: Add yalla upgrade --check, yalla upgrade --check --json, and yalla upgrade --yes.
Detect Homebrew, npm, npx, Scoop, WinGet, manual binary, and unknown install methods where practical.
For package-managed installs, report or run the package-manager upgrade command instead of overwriting files.
For manual installs, download from GitHub Releases, verify checksum/signature, and replace atomically.
Never auto-update silently during normal commands.
Tests cover each install method decision path.
userStories.notes: Self-update is allowed only for unmanaged/manual binaries.

userStories.title: Implement security and dependency verification gates
userStories.description: Add checks that protect users and agents from leaking secrets or shipping vulnerable builds.
acceptanceCriteria: Add govulncheck to the verification loop where available.
Add staticcheck and golangci-lint when configured.
Add tests that verify token and secret redaction in errors, debug logs, and dry-run output.
Add dependency review expectations for new third-party packages.
Document the minimum required checks before commit and before release.
userStories.notes: The CLI will handle production infrastructure credentials. Treat leaks as release blockers.

userStories.title: Implement curated command policy and naming conventions
userStories.description: Define how raw API operations become stable human and agent commands without sacrificing full coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: Document command naming rules for project, app, compose, database, server, settings, and provider domains.
Every curated command maps to one or more OpenAPI operation IDs.
Raw API coverage remains available for every operation even when a curated command exists.
Command help includes examples for human and --json usage.
Manifest output includes curated command to operation mappings.
userStories.notes: Use clear names. Do not optimize for clever short aliases.
